newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Viag unaffected by BT/MCI merger.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Viag unaffected by BT/MCI merger.

text.p: German mixed utility Viag AG, British Telecommunications Plc's partner in Germany, said that it is a passive observer in the mooted merger between BT and the U.S. telecoms firm MCI.
"Viag is not affected by the merger," Egon Muehlberger, press spokesman for the giant utility group, told Reuters over the weekend.

Cash-rich Viag has been keen to expand its telecoms interests and formed an alliance with BT to assist in efforts to crack the German telecoms market, over which Deutsche Telekom AG has a monopoly, after deregulation in 1998.

Muehlberger said a move to fuse BT and MCI would have very little impact on the existing partnership between BT and Viag, adding that Viag Interkom, its telecommunications subsidiary, already supplied MCI products in Germany through BT.
The spokesman said that if the merger was to have any effect on Viag's telecommunications business, it would be a positive one.
The merger between BT and MCI would form a true telecoms giant, with revenues of 38 billion dollars, 182,000 employees and a proforma market value of 64 billion dollars.
Only Japan's NTT and AT&T Corp would be bigger in the world.
In October, both Viag and BT were hit by the sudden departure of German utility RWE AG from their telecoms alliance. RWE left the alliance to link up instead with Veba AG and Cable & Wireless Plc.
